messages.author: 31c79caee221abb5
messages.subject: R/QTL for binary traits
parts:
Hi!

I would like to use R/QTL mainly for the analysis of ENU mutants which
usually have monogenic, dominant traits and we usually phenotype our
animals non-quantitatively. As far as I understood, the best way to
analyze the data would be

> result <- scanone(some_backcross, model="binary")

Everything works fine and I get a significant LOD Score which is in
consent with previous findings If I analyze backcrosses containing
mutant (phenotype = 1) as well as wildtype (phenotype = 0) animals.
However, if I only include mutant animals and no wildtypes I only get a
LOD Score of 0.
I tried to analyze the data by turning the genotype data of the mutants
around and pretending that these animals would have a phenotype = 0. If
I combine these two data sets I get results that fit our previous
findings, but I'm not sure is this is the "official" way to do it.
Is there a better way to analyze the data?

Thank you for your help!
Matthias

messages.author: f388084a0de67b60
messages.subject: Re: R/QTL for binary traits
parts:
Dear Matthias,

The binary trait analysis in scanone won't work in the case
that all individuals are affected are all are unaffected.
What it does, in essence, is split individuals according to their
genotype at a position and then compare the proportion of affecteds
in the different genotype groups.

If you are to look at affecteds only, you must study the genotype
data for some departure from Mendelian segregation, and R/qtl does
not have any facilities to do that properly.

regards,
karl
